basis: Collagen VI muscular dystrophy with weakness and contractures; respiratory failure reflects respiratory muscle weakness, without established intrinsic lung damage.
Severe peroxisomal disorder with CNS and hepatic disease; epiphyseal stippling is a major diagnostic skeletal feature. Ocular abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.
Cerebellar channelopathy causing episodic and progressive ataxia; central nystagmus, diplopia and vertigo do not establish separate eye or ear damage.
Glutamine metabolic disorders; severe developmental brain dysfunction or encephalopathy is characteristic across both listed subtypes, exceeding 30%.
Distal arthrogryposis with congenital joint contractures and skeletal abnormalities; facial and palatal morphology does not establish additional organ dysfunction.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder defining Leigh encephalopathy with cardiomyopathy; additional destructive myopathy frequency is unspecified.
Uterine and cervical malignancies arise in reproductive organs, outside the axes; no other organ damage is common across this umbrella.
Defining poikiloderma, contractures, myopathy and pulmonary fibrosis; hepatic and pancreatic dysfunction are variable and not established above 30% here.
Copper transport disorder with neurodegeneration and characteristic hair/skin disease; vascular dilation 80–99% and stenosis 30–79%; common skeletal abnormalities omitted at cap.
Splenic involvement by hairy cell leukemia, a mature B-cell leukemia/lymphoma; spleen belongs to the haematologic axis, not gastrointestinal.
Neuroendocrine tumor arising in parasympathetic paraganglia; usually nonsecretory. Ear and vascular involvement depend on the anatomical subtype.
Site-unspecified germ-cell tumor, predominantly reproductive in origin; no covered organ is shared by most cases. Extragonadal sites require site-specific labels.
Obstruction affects renal arteries; kidney parenchymal injury is not inherent, and ischemic nephropathy is a separately diagnosed consequence.
Childhood neurodegeneration; structural laryngomalacia and sensorineural hearing impairment each reported in 1/2 assessed patients. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
Trauma-related psychiatric disorder without defining direct damage to any covered organ.
Inherited abnormal hemoglobin affecting erythrocytes; generally asymptomatic or mildly anemic, without common extrahematologic damage.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, developmental impairment and brain abnormalities; isolated constipation does not establish direct bowel damage.
Neoplasms occupying kidneys or urinary collecting and outflow structures, all covered by the renal axis.
Immunodeficiency with autoinflammation and established bronchiectatic lung damage in 4/5 patients (80%); hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish organ dysfunction.
Inherited progressive skin pigmentation disorder; no established common damage outside skin.
Hamartoma of the breast; breast tissue is outside the organ axes.
Warm autoantibodies destroy red blood cells; dyspnea and palpitations reflect anemia. Heart failure is occasional, and bilirubin elevation does not establish hepatic damage.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with low estradiol and inhibin and elevated gonadotropins; gonadal hormone dysfunction belongs to metabolic_endocrine.
Inflammatory, immune-mediated airway disease with aspirin-triggered severe obstruction; airway involvement is defining.
Malignant tumor arising from peripheral nerve sheath; adjacent tissue invasion varies and does not define another commonly damaged organ.
